appearance_facts.fact: Title text reads 'Incidence of Condition A in US States'.
Vertical color bar labeled 'High' at the top and 'Low' at the bottom, with tick values 100, 80, 60, 40, 20, 0. The scale runs from pale yellow (high) to dark red/maroon (low).
Large central-south state polygon filled with very pale yellow, indicating a value near the top of the scale (approx. 90-100).
Northwest state polygon filled with dark maroon/red, indicating a value near the bottom of the scale (approx. 0-10).
Mountain state polygon filled with light gray, indicating no data or a neutral value distinct from the color scale.
Other states show a gradient from pale yellow (e.g., MT, ND, UT) to dark red (e.g., NY, GA, FL, MN), with some states in gray (e.g., CA, AZ, NM border, AR, AL).

printed_facts.fact: Scale: 0 (Low, dark red) to 100 (High, pale yellow). Ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100.
TX is labeled in the large pale yellow region. WA is labeled in the dark red region. CO is labeled in the gray region.
TX color corresponds to ~95-100. WA color corresponds to ~5-10. CO is gray (excluded/missing).
